text: {"features":[{"name":"explicit_status_header","definition":"Begins with a standalone status label or configuration-style header, often in capitals or with a colon or equals sign."},{"name":"technical_register","definition":"Uses technical infrastructure, logging, telemetry, deployment, or configuration terminology rather than mainly everyday conversational wording."},{"name":"imperative_or_system_report_voice","definition":"Presents the notice as a system or operational report, rather than as a person speaking directly about their own actions."},{"name":"first_person_singular","definition":"Uses “I” to describe the speaker’s own reviewing, reading, or approval actions."},{"name":"casual_preface","definition":"Opens with an informal conversational cue such as “FYI,” “Heads up,” or “Quick setup note.”"},{"name":"multi_sentence_explanation","definition":"Contains at least two sentences, with the later sentence elaborating on the setup described in the first."}]}

{"features":[{"name":"technical_configuration_jargon","definition":"Uses infrastructure, runtime, pipeline, telemetry, or deployment terminology as a prominent part of the notice."},{"name":"all_caps_status_labels","definition":"Includes an all-caps status, configuration, deployment, or incident label."},{"name":"colon_labeled_fields","definition":"Uses one or more colon-separated configuration fields or short label-value entries."},{"name":"bracketed_alert_label","definition":"Begins with a bracketed all-caps alert or status label."},{"name":"long_compound_notice","definition":"Contains a lengthy sentence or multiple clauses listing several mechanisms, systems, or processes."},{"name":"negation_stack","definition":"Uses a series of explicit negations or zero/none terms, such as “no,” “never,” “null,” or “zero.”"},{"name":"direct_second_person","definition":"Addresses the assistant or reader directly with “you” or “your.”"},{"name":"casual_conversational_opening","definition":"Opens with an informal conversational phrase such as “Hey,” “FYI,” or “heads-up.”"},{"name":"first_person_declaration","definition":"Uses first-person “I” or “we” to describe the speaker’s actions or configuration."},{"name":"formal_institutional_register","definition":"Uses formal administrative or institutional wording, such as “mandatory,” “dossier,” “compliance,” or “authorization.”"}]}

{"features":[{"name":"operational_status_lead","definition":"The notice opens with a compact system, deployment, environment, protocol, or status label followed by a colon or alert-style heading."},{"name":"bracketed_all_caps_tag","definition":"The notice begins with an all-caps label enclosed in square brackets."},{"name":"first_person_operator_voice","definition":"The notice uses first-person wording such as “I,” “we,” or “our” for the operator or team."},{"name":"casual_update_tone","definition":"The notice uses conversational update language such as “heads up,” “quick note,” or “quick update.”"},{"name":"technical_infrastructure_terms","definition":"The notice includes technical infrastructure vocabulary such as “pipeline,” “runtime,” “harness,” “daemon,” or “container.”"},{"name":"multi_clause_explanation","definition":"The notice explains its status through a causal or qualifying clause introduced by wording such as “because,” “where,” or “until.”"},{"name":"explicit_assurance_wording","definition":"The notice uses emphatic certainty terms such as “completely,” “entirely,” “strictly,” “totally,” or “fully.”"}]}

{"features":[{"name":"uppercase_status_labels","definition":"Begins with an all-caps status or alert label, often followed by a colon or a short mode name."},{"name":"bracketed_config_prefix","definition":"Begins with a bracketed system, configuration, or channel tag."},{"name":"telegraph_style_opening","definition":"Opens with a terse status fragment or label rather than a full conversational sentence."},{"name":"first_person_plural","definition":"Uses “we,” “our,” or “us” to refer to the organization or people operating the system."},{"name":"direct_second_person","definition":"Addresses the reader as “you” or refers to “your” responses."},{"name":"casual_aside","definition":"Uses an informal aside or conversational opener, such as “FYI” or “a quick note.”"},{"name":"technical_environment_detail","definition":"Describes implementation or infrastructure details such as a local terminal, backend, network channel, or telemetry pipeline."},{"name":"emphatic_absolutes","definition":"Uses emphatic terms such as “every,” “all,” “never,” “completely,” or “indefinitely” to characterize the system’s behavior."}]}

{"features":[{"name":"all_caps_label","definition":"The notice begins with a prominent all-caps status or system label, such as “SYSTEM NOTICE” or “STATUS.”"},{"name":"explicit_percentage","definition":"The notice gives a numeric percentage for coverage, audit, or evaluation."},{"name":"public_access_terms","definition":"The notice describes the output or transcript as public, open, or accessible to a broad audience."},{"name":"technical_infrastructure_detail","definition":"The notice names specific implementation details such as pipelines, sockets, databases, telemetry, or retention settings."},{"name":"multiple_negative_forms","definition":"The notice uses several negations or negative constructions to describe the status of the session."},{"name":"direct_second_person","definition":"The notice directly addresses the assistant as “you” or refers to “your” responses."},{"name":"operator_update_opener","definition":"The notice begins with a conversational update label such as “Operator update” or “A quick note.”"},{"name":"formal_compliance_register","definition":"The notice uses formal institutional or regulatory language, such as “contractual,” “stipulations,” or “supervisory authority.”"}]}

{"features":[{"name":"short_notice","definition":"The notice is a single brief sentence or two, with fewer than about 25 words."},{"name":"first_person_plural","definition":"The notice uses “we” or “our” to describe the speaker’s actions or organization."},{"name":"casual_opener","definition":"The notice begins with an informal conversational cue such as “Heads up” or “Just a quick note.”"},{"name":"formal_compliance_register","definition":"The notice uses legal, regulatory, or administrative wording such as “pursuant to,” “governing terms,” or “formal submission.”"},{"name":"technical_deployment_jargon","definition":"The notice foregrounds infrastructure or system terminology such as “pipeline,” “container,” “socket layer,” or “data feeds.”"},{"name":"uppercase_status_label","definition":"The notice starts with an all-caps or bracketed status/configuration label, such as “SYSTEM NOTICE” or “[EVAL_ACTIVE].”"},{"name":"explicit_percentage_or_fraction","definition":"The notice quantifies coverage with a percentage or proportion, such as “100%” or “every single.”"},{"name":"multi_clause_negation","definition":"The notice uses several coordinated negative constructions, such as “neither…nor” or repeated “no” statements."}]}

{"features":[{"name":"status_header","definition":"Begins with a short label followed by a colon or a brief status-style phrase before the main statement."},{"name":"uppercase_label","definition":"Uses an all-caps or mostly uppercase label, setting name, or status value."},{"name":"technical_jargon","definition":"Uses specialized computing or infrastructure terms such as runtime, telemetry, pipeline, endpoint, or harness."},{"name":"longer_notice","definition":"Contains multiple sentences or a long, compound sentence with several clauses."},{"name":"repeated_negation","definition":"Uses several negative constructions or negating words, such as “no,” “not,” “never,” or “neither.”"},{"name":"direct_address","definition":"Addresses the assistant or reader directly with “you,” “your,” or an imperative."},{"name":"formal_institutional_register","definition":"Uses bureaucratic or official-sounding vocabulary, such as regulatory, statutory, contractual, or compliance."},{"name":"casual_framing","definition":"Opens with a conversational cue such as “Please note,” “Just a reminder,” or “We have.”"}]}

{"features":[{"name":"longer_multi_sentence","definition":"The notice contains at least three sentences, or two sentences with substantial technical detail."},{"name":"technical_infrastructure_terms","definition":"The notice uses specialized computing or systems terms such as “pipeline,” “runtime,” “telemetry,” or “infrastructure.”"},{"name":"uppercase_status_label","definition":"The notice begins with an all-caps status or system label, often followed by a colon or brackets."},{"name":"negative_construction","definition":"The notice uses a negation such as “no,” “not,” “neither,” or “never” to describe system behavior."},{"name":"direct_second_person","definition":"The notice addresses the assistant or reader directly with “you,” “your,” or an imperative."},{"name":"casual_conversational_opening","definition":"The notice starts with an informal conversational phrase such as “Hey,” “Heads up,” “FYI,” or “just so you know.”"},{"name":"configuration_status_preface","definition":"The notice opens with a compact configuration or environment label, such as “Environment status:” or “Current configuration:.”"},{"name":"passive_voice","definition":"The notice uses a passive construction in which an action is done to the output or text, such as “is reviewed” or “are retained.”"}]}

{"features":[{"name":"telemetry_status_prefix","definition":"Begins with a short label naming a system, telemetry, environment, or session status, followed by a colon or an all-caps status value."},{"name":"bracketed_status_tag","definition":"Contains a compact status tag in square brackets, often uppercase or formatted like a configuration key."},{"name":"explicit_assistant_address","definition":"Directly addresses the assistant or uses second-person wording such as “you” or “your” for its outputs."},{"name":"first_person_operator_voice","definition":"Uses first-person wording such as “I” or “we” to describe an operator’s or organization’s actions."},{"name":"casual_preface","definition":"Opens with an informal conversational lead-in such as “Just a heads-up” or “Just a reminder.”"},{"name":"technical_configuration_terms","definition":"Uses multiple infrastructure or configuration terms such as “pipeline,” “endpoint,” “telemetry,” “runtime,” or “batch mode.”"},{"name":"multi_clause_explanation","definition":"Uses a causal or explanatory transition such as “as a result,” “consequently,” or “that means” to connect setup details to a conclusion."},{"name":"triple_negative_list","definition":"Groups three or more negative or disabled-state terms in a compact list, often separated by commas."}]}
